label: Unplanned weight change in recent weeks
sourceNote: DSM-5 MDD criterion 3; NIMH. Best asked weekly, not daily

label: Headache
sourceNote: NIMH: aches or pains, headaches

label: Aches, pains, cramps, or digestive trouble with no clear cause
sourceNote: NIMH: physical symptoms that don't improve with treatment

label: Body felt heavy
sourceNote: Commonly reported (more typical of atypical depression); not a core DSM-5 criterion

label: Irritable or short-tempered
sourceNote: NIMH: irritability, frustration; DSM-5 allows irritable mood in children and adolescents

label: Anxious or on edge
sourceNote: NIMH: persistent anxiety; DSM-5 'with anxious distress' specifier

label: Angry or snapped at people
sourceNote: NIMH: more anger or irritability

label: Withdrew from or avoided people
sourceNote: NIMH: isolating from family and friends

label: Cancelled or avoided plans
sourceNote: Commonly reported

label: Neglected responsibilities (work, bills, chores)
sourceNote: NIMH: neglecting responsibilities; DSM-5 requires impairment in functioning

label: Skipped self-care (washing, eating, dressing)
sourceNote: Commonly reported in more severe episodes

label: Difficulty getting through usual tasks
sourceNote: Daily functioning proxy

label: Thoughts of death, or of harming myself
sourceNote: Standard item in mood tracking. If anything other than 'None' is chosen, the app should show crisis resources (US: call or text 988) rather than only logging it. Not a substitute for care. DSM-5 MDD criterion 9

label: Took medication as planned
sourceNote: Only relevant if the user has a medication plan

label: Alcohol or other substances today
sourceNote: NIMH: increased alcohol or drug use can accompany depression

label: Exercise or movement
sourceNote: Context item; not a diagnostic criterion

label: Time outdoors / daylight
sourceNote: Context item

label: Stressful event today
sourceNote: Context item; helps link triggers to symptoms

label: Kept a regular routine (meals, wake and sleep times)
sourceNote: Context item

label: Social interaction
sourceNote: Context item. Read alongside the withdrawal items

label: Used a coping tool or reached out to someone
sourceNote: Context item; helps show what works

label: Overall mood
sourceNote: Quick summary rating

label: Overall symptom burden today
sourceNote: Quick summary rating

label: Overall functioning today (work, home, relationships)
sourceNote: Reverse-scored: higher is better

label: How many hours did you sleep last night?
crossRefNote: Short sleep (6 h or less) is the clearer risk; very long sleep is less certain. Time actually asleep, not time in bed. Quarter-hour steps. Ask "Is that right?" if under 2 or over 14.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: What time did you go to bed?
crossRefNote: Descriptive; the app computes day-to-day variation. Needs about 7 days of entries before showing a regularity score. Log bedtime and wake time (next item) so the app can show how much your schedule varies. Wake time may fall after midnight relative to bedtime.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: What time did you wake up?
crossRefNote: Descriptive; pairs with bedtime (H002). Second half of the sleep schedule spec (bedtime and wake time).
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How many glasses of water did you drink today?
crossRefNote: Plain water only. Glass size is a UI choice, not from the study. Cap at 20; no alert needed.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How much of today's food was whole or minimally processed?
crossRefNote: Whole foods: vegetables, fruit, legumes, whole grains, nuts, lean protein. A rough judgement is fine. Avoid scoring or shaming language.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: How many alcoholic drinks did you have today?
crossRefNote: One US standard drink is about a 12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, or 1.5 oz spirits. For 4 or more in a day, show a neutral note and support links; never block entry.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Mixed

label: How many caffeinated drinks did you have today?
crossRefNote: Roughly 100 mg of caffeine in a cup of coffee, less in tea or soda. Optional note above about 4 coffees (400 mg/day was the meta-analysis cut-off). Risk is for anxiety.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How many cigarettes (or nicotine uses) today?
crossRefNote: Count cigarettes, vaping sessions, or pouches as one use each. If the user is trying to quit, show a streak of low days instead of a warning.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: Did you use cannabis today?
crossRefNote: Private and non-judgemental. Includes smoking, vaping, and edibles. Treat answers as sensitive data. Risk is especially with psychosis.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: How many minutes did you exercise or move on purpose?
crossRefNote: Walking counts. Count only intentional movement, not just being on your feet. No upper-limit evidence in the reviews.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Strong

label: What kind of exercise did you do?
crossRefNote: Optional. Pick the main type. Show only when exercise duration is above 0.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: How many minutes did you spend outside in a park, garden, trail, or other green space?
crossRefNote: Nature means a natural setting such as a park, garden, trail or shoreline. The review counted 10 minutes or more.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: How far did you get out of the house today?
crossRefNote: Graded on purpose so a small step counts. Do not frame "did not go outside" as a failure. Avoiding the outdoors out of fear is itself an anxiety symptom.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How many minutes were you in bright light, such as daylight outdoors or a light box, today?
crossRefNote: Light-box sessions or time outside in daylight. The trials tested light-therapy devices, not ordinary daylight; morning timing probably matters most.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How many minutes did you meditate or do mindfulness practice?
crossRefNote: Seated meditation, guided audio, or mindful breathing all count. No established daily dose.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: How much time did you spend with other people today?
crossRefNote: Calls, video, or in person all count. Matches the "Social interaction" item in the condition lists.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How many hours of recreational screen time did you have today?
crossRefNote: TV, games, social media and streaming. Exclude work or school screens. Ask "Is that right?" above 16 h.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: Did you bathe or shower today?
crossRefNote: Any bath, shower, or full wash counts. Keep wording neutral and judgement-free. Do not show a streak counter that shames missed days. A marker, not a treatment.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How many minutes did you spend in a warm bath or soak?
crossRefNote: Optional. Warm, not scalding. Caution: the pilot used supervised baths at about 40 C, and some people had dizziness or a racing heart. People with heart conditions or low blood pressure should check with a clinician.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: How much basic self-care did you manage today (washing up, getting dressed, brushing teeth)?
crossRefNote: Small steps count. Complements the bathing item. A marker of functioning, not a treatment.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited

label: Did you take your medication as planned?
crossRefNote: Only shown if the user has a medication plan. After repeated "No", suggest contacting the prescriber; never advise stopping or changing doses.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Moderate

label: How regular was your routine today (meals, wake and sleep times)?
crossRefNote: Same wording as the routine item in the condition lists.
sourceNote: Evidence strength: Limited
